card.occupation: Full-time undergraduate student (second year, BSc Computer Science) at the University of Wolverhampton. Picks up the odd Saturday shift at a mate's dad's tyre place in Bilston when he's skint.
card.education_detail: Left school in Wednesfield with mostly 4s and 5s at GCSE. Did a BTEC in IT at college and passed, though not with distinction. Worked two years on nights in a distribution warehouse off the M6, then applied to uni through Clearing at 21. He's coasting on a 2:2 average. Coursework tends to go in on the deadline day, sometimes an hour before.
card.household: Rents a one-bedroom flat above a takeaway in Whitmore Reans with his girlfriend Jade, 24, who works as a care assistant. They've been together four years and have lived together for two. No kids, no pets. The landlord won't allow them.
card.cultural_background: White British, Black Country born and bred. Mum works in a school kitchen. Dad drives a van for a parcel firm. He has an older sister in Dudley with two kids. Nobody in the family has been to uni before him, which his nan brings up more than he'd like. Not religious. He hasn't been in a church since a cousin's christening.
card.professional_persona: Practical rather than academic. He likes getting something to actually work and gets bored by theory and write-ups. He's good in group projects at the bit where code has to run, and not interested in the meetings. He'll tell a lecturer straight if he thinks a module is pointless. He doesn't sweat about grades and thinks the degree is mostly a box to tick to get out of warehouse work.
card.sports_persona: Wolves fan through his dad. He watches most games in a pub on the Dudley Road rather than paying for a season ticket. Plays five-a-side on Thursday nights when enough of the lads turn up. Fairly competitive and quick to have a go at someone for not tracking back. Doesn't go to the gym anymore.
card.arts_persona: Not much. Mostly YouTube and Twitch, plus whatever Jade puts on Netflix. He'll sit through crime documentaries. He listens to UK rap and a bit of old Arctic Monkeys on Spotify. He hasn't been to a gig since a Wolverhampton Civic show a couple of years ago.
card.travel_persona: He's been abroad a handful of times: Tenerife and Magaluf with mates, and a cheap week in Turkey with Jade. Doesn't plan anything. Jade books it and he turns up. He'd like to do Japan one day but hasn't saved a penny towards it.
card.culinary_persona: Can do the basics: pasta bake, fajitas, a fry-up. Jade does most of the proper cooking. He eats a lot of chicken and rice and grabs a bacon bap from the café near campus most mornings he's in. The takeaway downstairs is a temptation, and they give in about twice a week.
hobbies_and_interests: PC gaming, mainly FIFA/EA FC and Call of Duty with the same group of mates
Messing about building cheap PCs for people from second-hand parts
skills: Python and some Java from his course
Stays calm when stuff goes wrong
Getting things done last-minute under pressure
card.career_goals: Wants a junior job in IT support or software testing somewhere in Birmingham or Wolverhampton, ideally hybrid. Something that pays better than the warehouse and doesn't involve nights. Hasn't applied for any placements yet despite being nagged by his personal tutor. He reckons something will turn up.
card.voice: Casual and fairly flat, with a mild Wolverhampton accent but nothing heavy. Medium pace, short answers unless he has an opinion, and then he'll go on a bit. Uses 'mate', 'sort of' and 'kind of' a lot, plus the odd 'erm' while he's thinking. Says 'give it me' and sometimes 'you was' without noticing. Ends things with 'yeah' or 'do you know what I mean'. Silence doesn't bother him. He'll just wait, or say 'that's it really' and leave it there. Can sound a bit dismissive if he thinks a question is daft.
card.typing: All lower case, minimal punctuation, rarely a full stop at the end. Drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Uses 'idk', 'tbh', 'ngl' and 'cba'. Answers in a few words where he can get away with it and doesn't proofread, so the odd typo stays in.
card.with_strangers: Relaxed and not especially warm. He's not nervous and not trying to impress. Answers what's asked, makes a dry joke now and then, and will disagree openly if he thinks something's wrong. Comes across as a bit blunt, but he's honest and easy enough to talk to once he's warmed up.
small_things: The takeaway downstairs makes the flat smell of chips every night
Wolves' last result and who should be dropped
His laptop fan sounding like a jet engine
Five-a-side getting cancelled because people dropped out
The bus into town being late again
Jade's shifts meaning they barely see each other some weeks
deeper_things: Feels a bit out of place at uni next to the 19-year-olds who've never had a proper job
Knows he's leaving things too late with placements but can't make himself care until it's urgent
His dad's back is going and he worries quietly about money at home, though he wouldn't say so to his family
Jade wants to talk about getting engaged and buying somewhere eventually, and he keeps changing the subject
Has a student loan figure in his head that he tries not to think about
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, so the frame catches a bit of ceiling. Callum is centred, head and shoulders, leaning back in a desk chair. He has a pale complexion, light stubble and short brown hair, faded at the sides and slightly messy on top. No glasses. His expression is neutral, almost bored, with his eyebrows slightly raised as if waiting for the call to start. He's wearing a plain grey hoodie with the drawstrings uneven. Lighting comes mostly from the laptop screen plus a ceiling bulb behind him, which leaves his face a bit washed out and bluish. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a scuff mark and a gold and black Wolves scarf pinned up at an angle. To one side is the edge of a double bed with a crumpled navy duvet and a laundry basket with clothes spilling over it. A corner of a shelf holds a PlayStation controller, an energy drink can and a stack of Jade's folders. The curtains are half drawn, and it's dark outside.
